findings.title: deleteCache deletes all cache rows for the credential without checking it is a Google credential or caches by userId
findings.body: The handler verifies the credential belongs to the user, then runs calendarCache.deleteMany by credentialId. This is scoped correctly for DB credentials, but the UI shows the Delete cached data action for any calendar integration where cacheUpdatedAt is set, and the mutation is not restricted to calendar credentials. Also, delegated/in-memory credential caches are keyed by userId (see getCachedAvailability), so deleting by credentialId does not clear the cache the user actually reads, making the 'Cache deleted successfully' toast misleading.

findings.title: deleteCache input accepts any credentialId without shared validation or authorization on the router
findings.body: The router inlines z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }) instead of a shared schema, and relies entirely on the handler's findFirst check. This is functionally guarded, but it is inconsistent with other calendar routes and gives no rate limiting or audit logging for a destructive operation on cache shared across the calendar sync pipeline.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with an empty array when no calendars are connected
findings.body: connectedCalendarsHandler passes all credentialIds to this method; when the list is empty Prisma's groupBy with credentialId in [] works but the call is an unnecessary DB round trip on every connectedCalendars query. More importantly, the query runs for every credential on each page load, adding a groupBy over CalendarCache that is not indexed on (credentialId, updatedAt), a performance concern on large tables.

findings.title: Cache status reports the most recent updatedAt across all keys, while the freshness of the cache used is per-key
findings.body: _max.updatedAt across all CalendarCache rows for a credential is shown as 'Last updated'. The row set includes entries for multiple timeMin/timeMax windows, and since @updatedAt is only bumped on upsert, this may show a timestamp that doesn't reflect whether the cache is expired (expiresAt) or stale. Status shown is not a true cache health indicator.

findings.title: updatedAt uses @default(now()) @updatedAt, but the migration uses NOW() with TIMESTAMP(3) and the schema comment is misleading
findings.body: The schema comment says the default is for legacy rows and raw inserts, but the migration backfills all existing rows with the migration time, so every legacy cache entry reports a 'last updated' value equal to deploy time, which is misleading in the UI. The migration also lacks the Prisma-managed @updatedAt behaviour in raw SQL, so any raw update path will not bump updatedAt.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty update payload, which may not bump updatedAt as intended
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}). Prisma's updateMany with empty data only bumps updatedAt if the field is @updatedAt, which it is for SelectedCalendar; but this touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential (including other event type scopes) on every cache refresh, adding write load on a hot path and changing updatedAt semantics that other code (UserWithCalendars.updatedAt) relies on. The PR notes concede this is unused in the frontend.

findings.title: Extra full-table write added on every availability cache refresh
findings.body: The new updateManyByCredentialId call runs after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, writing to all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential, even though the value is only used by nothing in the UI. This adds writes without a consumer and should be removed or justified.

findings.title: Intl format hardcodes en-US locale while the rest of the UI is localized
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) rather than the user's locale from useLocale, so non-English users see an English date format inside a translated sentence.

findings.title: Cache section shown only when cacheUpdatedAt is truthy, but Date is passed through JSON as string
findings.body: cacheUpdatedAt arrives from tRPC serialization (superjson or JSON) and may be a string, yet the prop is typed Date | null. new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) hides the type mismatch; with plain JSON the value is a string and the type is wrong. Type should reflect the wire format or the handler should guarantee Date.

findings.title: Delete cache mutation onSuccess does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: After deleting cache, cacheUpdatedAt in the connectedCalendars query remains stale, so the UI still shows the old 'Last updated' status until a refetch. The disconnect path invalidates queries but the delete cache path does not.

findings.title: Returns null when neither action is available, hiding the Alert/card actions layout
findings.body: When the dropdown returns null, the wrapping div with w-32 still renders in the calling component, leaving an empty reserved area; the previous code avoided rendering the wrapper. Minor layout regression.

findings.title: Disconnect action now shows for the error Alert card even when disableConnectionModification is not passed
findings.body: The error-state branch passes disableConnectionModification into CredentialActionsDropdown, but the old code hid the action only for delegation credentials and not for the disabled-modification case in that branch; behaviour change without test coverage.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only syntax and breaks on Linux
findings.body: sed -i '' -E ... treats the empty string as a backup suffix on BSD sed; on GNU sed it treats '' as the script and fails. The script is not portable and fails silently for Linux contributors.

findings.title: selectedCalendars select now loads updatedAt and googleChannelId for every session load
findings.body: findUnlockedUserForSession is on the hot session path; adding columns to the selectedCalendars select increases payload for each request even though the session does not use them.

findings.title: Comment says updatedAt doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache, now stale
findings.body: The TODO comment states updatedAt does not exist in CalendarCache, but this PR adds it. The comment and the orderBy logic should be updated to match.
